candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: human and veterinary castration studies reporting voice and behavior

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open supplementary behavioral and bioacoustic data

obstacles: 'Female character' has no single objective definition.
Pre/post-castration recordings with female controls are rare.
Effects depend strongly on species and age at castration.
rationale: Voice pitch can be tested for selected species using standard acoustics, while the character clause requires substantial and potentially misleading interpretation. Available evidence is fragmented and cannot support the universal 'all animals'.

operationalization: Use developmental dental series for pigs and lions to identify deciduous and permanent homologues and which tooth classes are replaced. Replacement outside lion canines or documented pig tooth replacement refutes the respective clause.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public juvenile and adult cranial CT scans and dental specimens

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species natural-history and anatomical accounts

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: veterinary and comparative dental-eruption studies

obstacles: 'Shed' must be distinguished from replacement, eruption, and wear.
Age-series specimen metadata may be incomplete.
rationale: Dental replacement is a standard anatomical trait in two well-studied mammals. Public specimen scans and veterinary literature provide age series sufficient to resolve both specific claims.

operationalization: No finite observation distinguishes a world in which nature never acts in vain 'so far as possible' from one containing failures, because any apparent counterexample can be redescribed as constrained possibility.
obstacles: 'In vain' and 'so far as possible' lack independent measurement criteria.
The qualification makes the universal resistant to counterexamples.
rationale: This is a teleological methodological assumption rather than a claim with a specified observable consequence. Its terms permit every biological outcome and therefore no dataset can discriminate it from rivals.

operationalization: Measure milk temperature at feeding and time to eruption of the first teeth in suckling mammals, controlling species, energy intake, growth, health, and maternal effects. Earlier eruption with hotter otherwise equivalent milk would support the prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: searchable neonatal nutrition and dental-eruption studies that may provide partial evidence

obstacles: Milk temperature is rarely retained as a measured exposure.
Temperature covaries with feeding method and milk handling.
Comparative tooth-eruption timing is not linked to individual feeding temperature.
rationale: The variables and intervention are clear, but existing public life-history data do not record milk temperature. A controlled animal study or purpose-built neonatal cohort appears necessary for a credible causal test.

operationalization: Estimate the age distribution of third-molar gingival eruption from population dental examinations and identify verified late-life eruptions. A central eruption age near twenty plus rare substantially later cases supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: public age-linked dental examination and tooth-status data

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: population dental-eruption studies and reports of delayed third-molar eruption

obstacles: Eruption, root growth, impaction, and delayed exposure after tooth movement must be distinguished.
Older adults with newly visible third molars are rare.
rationale: Third-molar eruption is routinely defined and recorded in dental examinations, with extensive age-stratified public data. Standard descriptive analyses can test the typical age, while literature cases address the late-age tail.
